stories.headline: Smart glasses boom faces tougher regulatory scrutiny in Europe
stories.subtitle: Reuters reports Europe's data protection board says Ray-Ban Meta-style glasses "facilitate covert recording" of bystanders, with regulators in Italy and Austria investigating school incidents and advocacy group NOYB urging coordinated restrictions. Expect customers to raise this on the floor.

stories.headline: Meta AI glasses go on sale in Thailand today
stories.subtitle: Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta smart glasses launch across Thailand from today, starting at 16,290 baht, with Meta AI now speaking Thai. Sold through authorized Ray-Ban and Oakley dealers nationwide — Meta's global rollout footprint keeps growing.

stories.headline: SanDisk named exclusive storage partner for Meta VR Glasses
stories.subtitle: SanDisk's official microSD Express cards and USB-C drives will arrive alongside the $1,299.99 VR Glasses in spring 2027. No pricing or capacities yet — expect customers to ask about expansion for the glasses' media-heavy use cases.

stories.headline: Glasses recorded conversations without 'Hey Meta'; Meta says it's fixed
stories.subtitle: Owners reported everyday chats landing in the Meta AI app even with wake-word-free listening off, and some saw the LED turn on unprompted. Meta told Android Authority the issue is resolved but never explained the cause. Point customers to reviewing and deleting voice logs in the app.

stories.headline: Malaysia launch: Gen 3 and Oakley Meta arrive Oct 20, from RM2,069
stories.subtitle: Four models hit Malaysia on Oct 20: Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 from RM2,119, Ray-Ban Meta Optics Gen 2 from RM2,209, Oakley HSTN at RM2,069 and Vanguard at RM2,589. Meta's global rollout keeps widening — a good sign if customers ask whether the glasses are still expanding.
